---
title: "Poster: Statistical Modeling, The Two Cultures"
---

For this project, me and Evan Toth tried to recap Leo Breiman's 2001 paper, "Statistical Modeling: The Two Cultures," and translate the main arguments into a poster. The poster contrasts data modeling and algorithmic modeling, then frames the practical takeaway as a problem-first approach to statistical work.

The central idea is not that black-box models are automatically better. It is that different goals demand different modeling cultures. Prediction, inference, causality, and interpretability do not always want the same tool.
